newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait stops withdrawals from state reserve.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait stops withdrawals from state reserve.

text.p: Kuwait has halted withdrawals from the state's foreign investment reserve which it used to finance the 1991 Gulf War and reconstruction after Iraqi occupation, a minister was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

"We returned $2 billion to the Reserve for Future Generations," al-Watan newspaper quoted Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan as telling parliament. "In October we stopped withdrawals from the reserve."

The reserve, built up by petrodollars invested abroad, was once valued at more than $100 billion but the state used much of it to pay for the Gulf War in which U.S.-led forces ended Iraq's seven-month occupation and for post-war reconstruction.
The English-language Arab Times said on Wednesday that according to official documents withdrawals totalled $80 billion while economists say the reserve is currently worth $40 billion.
Rodhan was responding to charges by MPs that the government had continued to withdraw funds from the reserve well after the Gulf War mainly to finance budget deficits.
MPs say the government needs parliament's approval to make withdrawals from the reserve. The government is obliged by law to inject 10 percent of its annual revenue into the reserve.

The government, enjoying added revenue from higher world oil prices, injected 1.742 billion dinars ($5.75 billion) last year into a state investment account which includes the reserve, balance of payment figures for 1996 show.
